slides.title: How file uploads work
slides.html:
Uploads

How file uploads work

  • Files are sent as multipart/form-data
  • express.json() can't read them
  • Multer parses the file into req.file
  • Text fields land in req.body

The request

POST /api/users/me/avatar
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=----X
 
------X
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="avatar"; filename="me.jpg"
Content-Type: image/jpeg
 
<binary image data>
------X--

slides.title: Multer with limits and a file filter
slides.html:
Multer

Multer with limits and a file filter

  • memoryStorage: keep it in RAM, send it on
  • Limit size and count
  • Allow only the types you expect

middleware/upload.js

import multer from "multer";
 
const ALLOWED = ["image/jpeg", "image/png", "image/webp"];
 
export const uploadImage = multer({
  storage: multer.memoryStorage(),
  limits: { fileSize: 2 * 1024 * 1024, files: 1 }, // 2 MB
  fileFilter: (req, file, cb) => ALLOWED.includes(file.mimetype)
    ? cb(null, true) : cb(new AppError(400, "Images only")),
});
 
// route: uploadImage.single("avatar")

slides.title: Storing images on Cloudinary
slides.html:
Cloudinary

Storing images on Cloudinary

  • Don't keep uploads on your server disk
  • Cloudinary stores, resizes and serves them
  • Save the url and public_id

services/cloudinary.js

import { v2 as cloudinary } from "cloudinary"; // uses CLOUDINARY_URL
export const uploadBuffer = (buffer, folder) =>
  new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    cloudinary.uploader.upload_stream({ folder },
      (err, result) => (err ? reject(err) : resolve(result))).end(buffer);
  });
 
const { secure_url, public_id } = await uploadBuffer(req.file.buffer, "avatars");

slides.title: Sending email with Nodemailer
slides.html:
Email

Sending email with Nodemailer

  • Create a transporter once
  • SMTP details come from .env
  • Use a real provider in production

services/email.js

import nodemailer from "nodemailer";
 
const transporter = nodemailer.createTransport({
  host: process.env.SMTP_HOST,
  port: Number(process.env.SMTP_PORT),
  auth: { user: process.env.SMTP_USER, pass: process.env.SMTP_PASS },
});
 
await transporter.sendMail({
  from: '"Blog" <no-reply@myblog.com>', to: user.email,
  subject: "Welcome 👋", html: `<h1>Hi ${user.name}</h1>`,
});

slides.title: Calling third-party APIs well
slides.html:
APIs

Calling third-party APIs well

  • Keys stay in .env on the server
  • Set a timeout
  • Check res.ok and handle failure
  • Retry only safe requests

utils/http.js

export async function callApi(url, options = {}) {
  const res = await fetch(url, {
    ...options,
    signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000), // 10 seconds
  });
  const data = await res.json().catch(() => null);
  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new AppError(502, data?.message || "Upstream failed");
  }
  return data;
}

slides.title: The Paystack payment flow
slides.html:
Paystack

The Paystack payment flow

1

Initialize

Your API calls Paystack with email, amount (kobo) and a reference

2

Redirect

Send the user to the authorization_url to pay

3

Verify

On return, your API verifies the reference with Paystack

4

Webhook

Paystack also POSTs charge.success to your webhook: trust that

slides.title: Initialize a transaction
slides.html:
Paystack

Initialize a transaction

  • Amount is in kobo (₦5,000 = 500000)
  • Use your own unique reference
  • Save a pending Payment first

controllers/payments.js

const reference = `bh_${Date.now()}_${req.user.id}`;
await Payment.create({ user: req.user._id, reference, amount: 500000, status: "pending" });
 
const { data } = await callApi("https://api.paystack.co/transaction/initialize", {
  method: "POST",
  headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY}`,
    "Content-Type": "application/json" },
  body: JSON.stringify({ email: req.user.email, amount: 500000, reference }),
});
res.json({ url: data.authorization_url });

slides.title: Verifying webhooks
slides.html:
Webhooks

Verifying webhooks

  • Use the raw body
  • Check the HMAC signature
  • Make it idempotent
  • Reply 200 fast

server.js (before express.json)

app.post("/api/webhooks/paystack",
  express.raw({ type: "application/json" }), async (req, res) => {
    const hash = crypto.createHmac("sha512", PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY).update(req.body).digest("hex");
    if (hash !== req.headers["x-paystack-signature"]) return res.sendStatus(401);
 
    const event = JSON.parse(req.body);
    if (event.event === "charge.success") {
      await Payment.updateOne({ reference: event.data.reference, status: "pending" },
        { status: "paid", paidAt: new Date() });
    }
    res.sendStatus(200);
  });
